user_review:
Yeni Lokanta is an unforgettable dining experience in Istanbul. Located near Taksim Square, just off the main Istiklal Street area, this Michelin-rated restaurant completely exceeded my expectations.

I visited with my family and tried the nine-course tasting menu. From the very first bite, every dish delivered a burst of flavors unlike anything I had experienced before. I have been to several Michelin restaurants in New York, and I can honestly say that the flavors at Yeni Lokanta surpassed many of them. Each course was creative, refined, and beautifully balanced.

The presentation of the dishes was also outstanding. From the appetizers to the main courses to the desserts, everything was elegant, artistic, and beyond five stars. The restaurant itself is cozy, quiet, and sophisticated, making it perfect for an intimate dinner where you can truly enjoy a conversation and hear each other.

The wine selection was excellent as well. They have an impressive cellar, and the wines were tasteful and paired beautifully with the meal.

I highly recommend Yeni Lokanta to anyone looking for a Michelin-rated restaurant near Taksim Square. It is very close to being a Michelin-starred experience, and in my opinion, it should be on every food lover’s bucket list when visiting Istanbul.

address: Levent, Nisbetiye Cd No:13, 34330 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Efendy İstanbul - Levent, Nisbetiye Cd No:13, 34330 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
We knew Efendy. For years it anchored the dining scene on Elliott Street, Balmain, a short walk from home. When it closed its Sydney doors, something felt unfinished. So we finished it properly, flying 16,000 kilometres to sit at Chef Somer Sivrioglu’s table in Istanbul.

It was absolutely worth it.

The room sets the tone immediately: warm terracotta walls, lush greenery spilling in from every corner, a softness that feels both ancient and considered. This is not a restaurant trying to look Turkish. It simply is.

Kemal, our host, is the kind of front-of-house presence that elevates a meal from excellent to memorable. Warm, knowledgeable, and genuinely invested in your experience, he guided us through the tasting menu with the ease of someone who loves the food as much as the kitchen does.

The dishes themselves reflect Somer’s gift for reimagining the Anatolian pantry.

This is modern Turkish cooking with real roots. Not fusion. Not nostalgia. Something rarer: a chef in full command of his own tradition.

Efendy left Balmain. We followed. No regrets whatsoever.

user_review: The service is excellent, with the friendly smiles and complimentary after-meal treats that every customer would appreciate. I do have one complaint: please fix the door; someone might accidentally open it and injure themselves. We went because of the positive reviews on Google, but it wasn't as good as they hyped up. The bread, the chicken, everything... was incredibly greasy, like dry oil. The sauces were too little for me, and of course, the greasiness made eating half the burger quite uncomfortable. Don't believe anyone who says it didn't bother you, because the bread tasted like regular bread made from regular flour and was very greasy. We asked for gloves, but the greasiness was visible through the fingertips. We ordered fries to share, but they came as a set menu. They apologized and wanted to change them, but it was fine, they just ended up wasted on our plates. We ordered iced tea, peach, and cola. The fries were really generous and seasoned; they weren't like homemade fries, just regular store-bought fries, you know, very greasy. Of course, all that greasy not only upset our stomachs but also made us feel heavy and sleepy, so you can imagine the rest. I didn't check the restrooms, but the place seemed clean, so I can't really say for sure about that, I didn't walk around and look. The biggest pluses were the good service and the complimentary tea and coffee. In total, we paid 600₺ for everything. Another plus was that the menu was a bit cheaper than typical burger places.

user_review:
Kaveka is a decent option in Taksim, especially because it’s one of the very few places that offers kunafa, other desserts, and hookah all in the same spot. That alone makes it convenient if you’re looking for dessert and shisha together without moving around.
The prices are fair for a Taksim restaurant, not cheap but reasonable compared to many nearby tourist-focused places. The menu has a good variety of desserts, and the kunafa option is a plus since it’s not easy to find in this area.
Atmosphere is nice and suitable for sitting and relaxing, especially in the evening. Service is okay nothing exceptional, but acceptable.
Overall, it’s a good stop if you want dessert and hookah in Taksim, but there’s still room for improvement in consistency and experience, which is why I’d rate it 3 stars.

user_review:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Amazing Seafood & Hospitality!

I visited this lovely restaurant in Istanbul and had an absolutely wonderful experience! 🇹🇷🐟 The seafood was incredibly fresh and delicious—perfectly cooked and full of flavor, easily some of the best I’ve had in the city.

What truly made our visit special, though, was the owner! He was so warm, kind, and incredibly generous. 🤗💛 Not only was service attentive, but he surprised us with free treats—traditional Turkish tea, delightful sweets, fresh nuts, and even water—all on the house! Such thoughtful touches made us feel like honored guests, not just customers.

The atmosphere was lovely, the food outstanding, and the hospitality unmatched. If you are in Istanbul and love seafood, you simply must come here. We left happy, full, and with huge smiles. 10/10, highly recommended! 🍤🍰☕️

user_review:
I had breakfast at Mr Simone in Istanbul, and it was honestly one of the most delicious breakfasts I have ever had. The food tasted incredibly fresh, flavorful, and truly homemade, which made the whole experience feel warm and authentic.

What I loved most was the homemade concept behind the dishes. Everything felt like it was prepared with care and attention to detail, giving it a unique and comforting touch that is hard to find.

One thing to keep in mind is that the portions are very generous, so make sure to check the size of what you’re ordering before placing your order. It’s great value for money, but you may end up ordering more than you can finish!

If you’re looking for a memorable breakfast experience in Istanbul with amazing homemade food, Mr Simone is definitely worth a visit.

If you're in Beylikdüzü and looking for fried chicken delivery or pizza, this place is definitely worth trying:

🍗 Chicken (drumsticks, wings & strips) — crispy outside, juicy inside, full of flavor
🍟 Fries & onion rings — perfectly fried, not oily
🌯 Wraps — fresh and well filled
🍕 1 kilo pizza — LOADED with toppings, not just dough — very satisfying

What stood out most is the portion size and consistency — you really get value for your money.

For anyone searching pizza delivery in Beylikdüzü or fried chicken in Istanbul, Kiloviç is a solid choice.

Definitely ordering again.

description: İSKENDER Kuruluş 1867 - Sinanpaşa, Süleyman Seba Cd. No:10, 34357 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Without a doubt, this was my best meal in Istanbul. Iskender completely redefined what kebab means to me. I ordered one portion, and everything was outstanding—the meat, the bread, the sauce, and the garnishes were all exceptional. I highly recommend this place!

There’s a saying that stays with you after reading it: “Tradition is not about preserving the ashes, but keeping the fire alive.” That idea is clearly the guiding philosophy here, and it shows not as marketing language, but as something that feels genuinely lived in.

The restaurant presents its 157-year heritage not as a distant historical claim, but as an active practice. The emphasis is on continuity—on keeping methods, values, and a distinctive sense of identity intact while still serving something relevant at the table today. That intention comes through in the experience itself: this is döner treated less as fast food and more as a disciplined craft, shaped by restraint rather than embellishment.

What stood out most during lunch was the confidence in simplicity. The meat—sourced from their own production—arrives with a clarity of flavor that doesn’t feel engineered or overworked. There’s no reliance on marinades or heavy seasoning; just salt, technique, and patience. Even the broader process, from sourcing to the charcoal used for cooking, is presented as part of a closed, self-reliant system, and it’s hard not to respect the consistency that produces.

The result is a meal that feels deliberate in every sense. Not flashy, not trying to reinterpret döner into something unfamiliar, but instead insisting on doing the traditional version exceptionally well—and letting that be enough.

user_review: Spectacular meal - we randomly went to this and had such a stand out meal - the winter tabbouleh was full of flavour and was refreshingly citrusy truly a display of winter produce, the kibbe was delish (and small bite size portions) , land was tender fall off bone and very well paired with their grains, infused rosemary olive oil with their soft flat breads. The winter bulgur pancakes reminded me of Chinese leek pancakes and were well paired with a mint yoghurt. The black eyed pea and chard salad was also delish and I enjoyed the Lebanese take on aromatics like a gentler rendition of fried shallots. wish we came with more people so we could try more dishes. Charming mid century modern vintage decor and really lovely, kind and attentive service (there’sa nice separate bar area too) - I highly recommend this hidden gem

user_review:
The largest daily market in western Istanbul is a vibrant world of its own.
It’s a place where colors, scents, and sounds blend into a lively symphony of city life. Stalls overflow with fresh, sun-kissed fruits and vegetables — each one perfectly arranged by proud local vendors who greet you with warm smiles. You’ll find rows of high-quality clothing, handmade goods, spices, and nearly everything you could ever need for everyday life. The air is filled with the aroma of ripe figs, roasted nuts, and freshly baked bread. Walking through the market feels like stepping into the beating heart of Istanbul — bustling, authentic, and irresistibly full of life.

We had an absolutely wonderful experience at Sakhalin Istanbul. I chose this place for my birthday dinner, and I can honestly say we left feeling completely satisfied and happy. From start to finish, everything about our visit exceeded expectations.

The food was exceptional — each dish was beautifully presented, bursting with flavor, and clearly made with fresh, high-quality ingredients. Every bite was a delight, and it really felt like the chefs put care and thought into every detail.

What made the evening even more special was the staff. They were incredibly friendly, warm, and attentive, making us feel welcomed and valued throughout the entire dinner. Their genuine hospitality added so much to the experience and made the night feel personal and memorable.

The ambiance of the restaurant is elegant, stylish, and cozy at the same time. It created the perfect setting for a celebration, making the evening feel truly special. Whether it was the lighting or the overall design, everything contributed to a refined yet relaxed atmosphere.

Overall, our experience at Sakhalin Istanbul was flawless. From the food and drinks to the service and atmosphere, everything came together beautifully. Choosing this place for my birthday was the perfect decision, and we would absolutely love to return. It’s a restaurant that not only satisfies your taste buds but also leaves you with warm, happy memories ✨

user_review:
Good for Privacy, but Priced at a Premium

We visited the VIP lounge at Huqqa with friends. The lounge access starts at $150, which includes a basic welcome plate of fruits, chocolates, and mixed nuts. Be aware that everything else—including hookah, any food orders (we tried the pasta and chicken sandwich), and even coffee—is an additional charge.

While the service was excellent and the staff were very friendly, the final bill can quickly add up. We ended up paying around $300 for what felt like very little food. The lounge is a great choice if you value privacy above all else, but be prepared for the steep pricing.

name: Mr.Hamza Beylikdüzü
address: Cumhuriyet Mahallesi Onur Sokak Kameroğlu Metrohome, Cumhuriyet, Sitesi L12, 34520 Beylikdüzü/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Mr.Hamza Beylikdüzü - Cumhuriyet Mahallesi Onur Sokak Kameroğlu Metrohome, Cumhuriyet, Sitesi L12, 34520 Beylikdüzü/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review: Generally, these types of boutique establishments are known for their delicious food and have branches in upscale districts of Istanbul, so I decided to try this place with high expectations. First of all, the restaurant is divided into two sections: indoor and outdoor seating. The outdoor area is like a winter garden, enclosed but cold without any heaters, while the indoor area has a stable temperature. The restaurant is very stylish and modernly designed. There is one staff member who handles both the cash register and orders; he is a very friendly and polite gentleman. You can access the menu via QR codes on the tables. While reviewing the options on the menu to order, I thought the prices were for the entire menu, as there was no indication of this. However, once I decided on my order, the staff member informed us that these prices were only for the hamburger, and that fries and a drink would have to be charged separately. We could also purchase fries and a drink for an additional 165₺, which is more economical than buying them separately. There are two points that bother me about this. Firstly, I understand that drinks aren't included in the menu price at most competing companies, but I find it ridiculous that fries are charged separately. Also, there's no informative mention of this on the menu; the staff only informing us about it right at the time of ordering feels like they're forcing us to pay. Regarding the taste, I ordered a cowboy burger, and it took about 10 minutes to prepare and serve. While the items on the menu are 90g starters, I ordered a 180g one, and frankly, it seemed small to me. Since it's a closed burger, it's a bit difficult to eat, so I asked for an extra knife and cut it in half. Because it's cooked closed, it's quite hot, so you should be careful while eating it. The bread was nicely cooked; the top was thin, but the bottom was a little thick. The most negative thing about the bread was that it was quite unsalted, which I noticed even though I'm not someone who craves salt. The ingredients in the burger were cooked very well, but you're eating a meat burger, so you want to taste the meat. However, in this burger, both the meat and the bun were very bland, and the meat lacked flavor. I don't want to name names, but the taste at most well-known burger places is far better than this. The fries weren't crispy; they seemed like they had been sitting around for a while because they were soft. The seasoning and flavor of the fries were good, but their soft state made them unpleasant to eat. After the meal, I asked the staff if they offered complimentary tea and if smoking was allowed in the outdoor seating area. When they said I could smoke outside, I requested that they offer complimentary tea there as well. My disappointment continued in this regard. If I were a shopkeeper, I would have said we ran out of tea instead of offering it to a customer, because the tea they offered was in terrible condition; it looked like it had been sitting in the kettle all day. I took one sip and stopped. When I went to the cashier to pay the bill at the end of the day, the staff asked if I was satisfied. I told them I wasn't, that I'd experienced better places. They told me I could write a review about the aspects I didn't like, and that they would take it into consideration. Because of all this, I felt the need to write such a detailed review. Frankly, when you pay close to 1400 lira for two hamburger menus, you expect to leave the table satisfied, but the only thing I can say about this place is that it will be my first and last visit. Both the pricing policy is expensive, and the quality and taste of the products offered don't justify those prices. The 2 stars I gave the place are due to the concept, cleanliness, and the attitude of the staff who served us. If you're thinking of going there just to try it out, I wouldn't recommend it, but the final decision is, of course, yours.

The food was delicious and the service from the staff was genuinely good. However, the hosting and table management were very disappointing.

We specifically requested a table by the sea, but were told that all tables were fully reserved. We respected that and stayed at another table. The issue is that we finished our entire meal, and throughout all that time more than four seaside tables remained completely empty.

The hosts could have easily managed the situation better by seating guests temporarily until the reserved customers actually arrived. Instead, the tables stayed unused while paying customers were denied the experience they came for.

Great food and good service were unfortunately overshadowed by poor client management at the entrance.

user_review:
Das Haus des Doners on the Asian side of Istanbul offers a solid fast-food döner experience. You can select how many grams of protein you want (they have options like 100 g, 150 g, 200 g), and add the usual toppings — tomato, lettuce, red cabbage, onion, pickles.
Prices are reasonable for Istanbul, though some reviewers say the bread (lavaş/yufka) is thin or not ideal, and that portion sizes don’t always feel worth what you pay.
The place is comfortable, service is okay, though sometimes slower.
Overall the food is tasty and the concept works, though it doesn’t always outperform other döner spots in Beşiktaş or Kadıköy.

user_review:
I recently visited Telgrafhane, and it was a delightful experience overall. The interior is beautifully decorated with a cozy yet stylish vibe, making it a perfect spot to relax and enjoy some treats. The display of pastries and desserts is impressive, with a variety of choices that not only look fantastic but taste delicious too.

One of the highlights was the view of the Bosphorus, which adds a unique charm to the cafe, especially if you manage to get a table by the window or sit outside. The outdoor seating allows you to fully appreciate the beautiful scenery, making the experience even more enjoyable.

While everything was pleasant, there were a few minor aspects that could be improved. However, I would still highly recommend Telgrafhane for anyone looking for a lovely cafe experience in Istanbul. Definitely worth a visit for the view alone!

user_review:
This is a place where you eat with your hands — no cutlery needed, and that’s part of the charm. It’s an authentic spot in Beykoz, always busy, which is a great sign of quality. The fish is delicious and fresh, and the prices are very reasonable.

The calamari is excellent, but honestly, whatever you order, you won’t regret it. They have plenty of staff and the service is friendly and attentive.

If you’re a seafood lover, this place is definitely worth a visit. 🐟

As for dessert — that’s their weaker point. The halva was tasty, but the other sweets we tried didn’t quite hit the mark.

name: Mikla
address: The Marmara Pera, Asmalı Mescit, Meşrutiyet Cd. No:15, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Mikla - The Marmara Pera, Asmalı Mescit, Meşrutiyet Cd. No:15, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Mikla is definitely one of the go to places for western dining in Istanbul !  Food, presentation & service were excellent and exceeded our expectations.

The restaurant is on the top level of the Hotel Pera 77, and commands a lovely view of Istanbul and the Bosphorus Bridge.  We booked online and was lucky to get a table on the Ramadan weekend.

To start, service was impeccable.  Our server was the one of the chefs and was able to explain the menu in details.  There is a 3 courses set and a 6 courses tasting menu to choose from.  We opted for the 3 courses which was definitely the right choice as there were starters on the house, and the portions were relatively large for fine dining.

Our starters- mushroom soup - was oozing with the flavors of mushroom and absolutely perfect for a cold rainy night.  The octopus was crunchy fresh and was topped with a refreshing sauce.  Both were very well seasoned prepared.

The  main courses - we ordered dry aged beef, and grilled swordfish which was cooked to perfection!  Up to this point, every thing was so delicious.

Dessert - We had berries ice cream, and saffron ice cream.  not sure if we were too full, or we had equally high expectations, could be better.  One was too sour, and the other too sweet.

Overall, we were quite pleased with the dinner- although it was slightly on the pricey side . On departure, we noticed it has just been awarded with a Michelin one star.  Congrats!

description: Meşale Cafe &restaurant - Büyükşehir, Başak Sokağı No:4, 34520 Beylikdüzü/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Marhaba 👋

I wanted to share my experience at a restaurant that I recently visited, which I think you might find interesting. The restaurant is located beside the bazaar and has a typical Turkish design, which adds to its charm and authenticity.

During my visit, I had the pleasure of trying their signature dish, the iskandar kebab, which was absolutely delicious. The meat was tender and well-seasoned, and it was served with a range of flavorful condiments and sides. I also tried their Turkish coffee, which was strong and rich in flavor, making it the perfect complement to the meal.

Aside from the great food, the restaurant also offers entertainment. While I was there, there was a traditional Turkish musician playing live music, which added to the ambiance and made the experience even more enjoyable.

Before you decide to visit, I would recommend checking their prices to ensure that it fits within your budget. Overall, I had a fantastic experience at this restaurant and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for an authentic Turkish dining experience.

description: Van Kahvaltı Beşiktaş - Sinanpaşa, Çelebi Oğlu Sk. No:35/A, 34353 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
I accidentally stumbled upon breakfast street. I thought this was a branch of Van Kahvalti Evi but I don’t think it is.

First, I am not from Türkiye nor have I ever been to Van, so I cannot judge on the authenticity of this breakfast.

I ordered the lowest tier breakfast, which was listed as 780 lira (for two).

The food I received was not exactly the food that was advertised, but in a good way. I wanted to try Muhlama which was in the second tier so I was delighted to receive it instead of something else. They also gave me kavut (usually stone ground millet/flour with butter, milk) and havuc tarator.

The honey was delightful with the salty cheese. The grilled olives were my favorite! The menemen was pretty good!

The only thing I could definitely distinguish as Van was the kavut, but again, I’m not from Van so I don’t know for sure.

The service was excellent. At the end, to my surprise, they had given me one portion of the breakfast and charged me half the price. I was very pleased with that!

Thank you for a positive experience.

user_review:
I recently visited Puu Fu, and it was an amazing experience. The place is cozy, calm, and beautifully decorated, making it the perfect spot to relax. The staff are very polite and welcoming, which makes the visit even more enjoyable.

Their Japanese cakes are the highlight — soft, light, and incredibly delicious. Each slice is freshly made and has a unique flavor that you don’t find easily in Istanbul. You can really taste the quality and effort they put into their desserts.

If you love Japanese-style treats or just want to try something different, Puu Fu Cafe is a must-visit. I’ll definitely be returning to try more of their cakes!

address: Ortaköy, Portakal Ykş. Cd. No:2, 34347 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Harbi Adana Ocakbaşı - Ortaköy, Portakal Ykş. Cd. No:2, 34347 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
The Adana shish was decent, however everything around it was not great. I have been in Adana and had plenty of Adana kebab there and all the condiments and appetizers were just off.
The bread was served cold, for such an expensive place it should not be pre made. All the appetizers were lacking seasoning and were pre made. Even the ezme and coban sallad had odd och lacked seasoning.
Another really disappointing part was that our waiter was so unengaged. We did not get any menu's, he was not really accomodating (the restaurant was empty (6 other people there in total) so I dont understand why everything took so long and why when we asked for something he started walking around other tables until he did anything). Er had to ask for everything, so odd that there are no menu's and if they dont have them, at least the waiter could explain the options, it felt like he was forced against his will to be there.
For 2000tl (2 people that did not order anything special) it is not enough that the shish is decent. The rest must be good too, especially if they call themselves an Adana ocakbasi, and that included service and food. Start with changing up the bread and cooking it fresh, same with salads and other appetizers that are always included wherever you go in Adana, they must taste fresher and be more well made.
The interior looked nice, and that was it.
I would not recommend making the effort to go there, really mid and Turkiye is filled with decent places around every corner.

name: Salt Fried Chicken
address: Sinanpaşa, Şair Nedim Cd. No:46/A, 34357 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Salt Fried Chicken - Sinanpaşa, Şair Nedim Cd. No:46/A, 34357 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Salt Fried Chicken in Beşiktaş is a great place to try a unique and trendy take on fried chicken and burgers. The concept is different from typical fast-food spots, which makes the whole experience feel fresh and memorable.

The restaurant itself is a bit small, which is one of the reasons it tends to get crowded quickly. It is very popular, so there is usually a long line. When you arrive, they take your name and give you a number, and once a table becomes available, they call your number so you can be seated. The wait can be a little long, but the food is definitely worth it.

The chicken was absolutely delicious, and the whole experience felt special, from the presentation and packaging to the variety of sauces that come with the meal.

In my personal opinion, the prices are a bit higher than expected, probably because of the popularity and hype surrounding the place. However, it was still a fun and tasty experience that I’m glad I tried.

Overall, I would definitely recommend Salt Fried Chicken if you are in Beşiktaş and want to try something different and trendy.

address: Hüseyinağa, Sahne Sk. No:25, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Tarihi Degustasyon Ocakbaşı - Hüseyinağa, Sahne Sk. No:25, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Our family had an absolutely outstanding dining experience. From the moment we arrived, the hospitality was exceptional and the staff made us feel genuinely welcome.

We started with several traditional mezes, including hummus, haydari, and ezme, all of which were fresh, flavorful, and perfect with the warm bread and fresh herbs served at the table. The parsley, basil, and lemon were a wonderful touch and added so much freshness to the meal.

For our main course, we enjoyed the Adana kebab, lamb chops, and the mixed kebab platter. Everything was cooked perfectly over charcoal and packed with flavor. The Adana kebab had just the right amount of spice, the lamb chops were tender and delicious, and the mixed platter was incredibly generous, featuring additional grilled meats and lamb loin that were equally outstanding. In fact, we ordered more food than we realized because everything sounded so good!

What truly set this restaurant apart was the service. The staff was attentive, friendly, and eager to make sure we had a memorable experience. To top off an already amazing meal, they treated us to Turkish tea, fresh watermelon, and complimentary kadayıf for dessert.

The food was exceptional, the portions were generous, and the hospitality was unforgettable. This was one of our favorite meals in Istanbul and one of the highlights of our trip. We would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic Turkish cuisine, outstanding service, and true Turkish hospitality.

I called to give feedback, but was met with resistance, extremely poor customer service, a passive aggressive rude employee/owner and an offensively false defence that ‘stale’ was not possible as they make each order from scratch - i would have believed that had it not arrived in the blink of an eye and didnt trust my ability to tell the difference between stale and fresh :). user_review:
Hidden in the heart of Besiktas, Mahal Meze & Meyhane feels less like a restaurant and more like a place you somehow wish you had discovered earlier.

This is not your typical meyhane. It’s intimate, almost boutique in scale, where every detail feels intentional. The real highlight, though, is the menu—filled with creative, unexpected mezes you won’t easily find elsewhere. The kind of dishes that make you pause for a second because you’ve genuinely never tasted anything quite like them before.

The atmosphere is warm and effortlessly nostalgic, elevated by a beautifully curated Atatürk corner that adds a deeper sense of character and meaning to the space. It’s subtle, but it changes the way you experience the night.

Come for the rakı, stay for the conversation, and leave with a list of flavors you’ll be thinking about long after.

user_review: We came to this lovely restaurant under the Galata Bridge for lunch with a small baby and the food, service and attention to details especially our baby was out of this world. The prices were fair and we were able to choose a fish size to our liking fresh out of the Bosporus. view was great overlooking the water and Blue Mosque with the sound of ferries passing by. The jumbo prawn entree was really good and when seafood is this fresh, you don't need a lot more than just garlic and mushroom as seasoning. The star of the show, the salt crusted seabream, thank you Azzat (sorry if I spell it wrongly!) for the show and the fish, nicely deboned! Thank you for making our holiday in Istanbul that much more special!

user_review:
I had higher expectations before visiting this restaurant. Ajvar was one of the most delicious one I’ve ever tried. Soka was delicate, too.

We tried three different types of meatballs.
Pljeskavica, Güveçte Kaymaklı Cevapi, and Mostar Köfte. I liked the Mostar köfte most.
I was expecting just a bit better flavors from each meatballs, but all consisted very much alike seasoning.

Prices are reasonable, service is okay, the atmosphere is very authentic.

Just so you know, from January 30, 2026 and on, you don’t have to pay any kuver, or service fee. This law is officially announced by the Ministry of Trade and Commerce They tried to charge, but we didn’t pay. You have all the right to object.

Overall score 3.9/5 for a Balkan Restaurant

name: Trabzon Sofrasi
address: Atatürk cad no :129, Yenibosna Merkez, 34100 Bahçelievler/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Trabzon Sofrasi - Atatürk cad no :129, Yenibosna Merkez, 34100 Bahçelievler/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
I have become a regular customer of this restaurant, and there are many reasons why I keep coming back. One thing I always notice is how organized everything is. The staff work in a coordinated way, the restaurant is clean, and the service is usually very fast. These small details show me that the management is doing a good job. It is not easy to maintain this level of organization every day, especially in a busy restaurant.

The atmosphere is also nice and comfortable. Whether you come alone or with friends, it is a pleasant place to sit and enjoy your meal. The restaurant is clean, the tables are well arranged, and the overall ambiance makes customers feel welcome.

Today I visited on a Saturday. Since weekends are usually busy, I understand that some menu items may sell out. Unfortunately, many of the dishes I wanted to order were not available when I arrived. Because of that, I ended up ordering a simple dürüm. It was okay, but it was not what I was hoping to eat today. I was looking forward to trying some of the other menu options.

Even though I was disappointed by the limited availability of food today, I still had a positive experience overall. The staff remained polite and attentive, and the service was as fast as always.

One thing I really enjoyed was the sütlaç. It was fresh, tasty, and a perfect way to finish the meal. I would definitely recommend trying it if you visit.

Overall, I highly recommend this restaurant. Good management, clean environment, fast service, and friendly staff make it a place worth visiting. I just hope more menu items are available during busy weekends because many customers come specifically for those dishes.

user_review:
This restaurant, boasting a breathtaking view of the Bosphorus, offered one of my best dining experiences in Istanbul. The service was exemplary, with the staff changing our plates and cutlery multiple times without being intrusive, and providing helpful advice on menu items.

We sampled their Kofte, Fish, and Hamsi. However, it's worth mentioning that the fish prices were not stated in the menu, which may be a point to note for potential diners. Despite this, the food was enjoyable, though not extraordinary, being about average in terms of quality.

The cost is on the higher end of the spectrum. For three of us, including a 700cc Raki and three Mezze, the bill amounted to 2300 TL. However, when considering the high-quality service, the enjoyable food, and the fantastic view of the Bosphorus, it was certainly a worthwhile experience.

user_review: My parents and I were staying at the Conrad and decided to have dinner here after arriving late in the evening. The atmosphere, food and cocktails were superb. The service, however, was appalling. We ordered the Chef Special Sushi and the Beef Bulgogi, along with three cocktails. After 45 minutes, my mother asked if the food was arriving soon. The waitress was dismissive and rude and simply stated that replied that the beef takes 30 minutes to cook. After enquiring about the sushi, we found out it was not even ordered. The waitress did not ever get back to us even after the food was served. Being a restaurant/bar at a five star hotel, one of the most elite hotels of the Hilton chain, I find this bitterly disappointing. I am a Hilton Honors member who has repeatedly chosen this chain, never had I ever received service like this. I hope this can be addressed, as the food and the drinks were exceedingly well delivered.

Unfortunately, our experience at Isan Meyhane was very disappointing. While we expected a pleasant evening, the service and overall experience fell far below expectations.
The staff were not welcoming or attentive. Every time we requested something, we had to ask several times before it was brought to our table, and when we raised concerns, our feedback was simply ignored.
The food quality was poor and did not justify the prices. On top of that, it felt like we were constantly being asked to pay extra for almost everything. What was most disappointing was finding an additional charge for turnip juice (şalgam) on our bill without anyone informing us beforehand or asking for our approval.
We left feeling that the focus was more on charging customers than providing good hospitality. Sadly, this experience ruined what was supposed to be an enjoyable evening. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and improves both the service and transparency.

description: Konyalı Ferdi Usta Ortaköy - Mecidiye, Muallim Naci Cd. No:25/A, 34347 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
We had dinner here tonight as a group of four, and it was truly an outstanding experience from start to finish. We ordered several appetizers, the Fattoush salad, bone marrow, and the large mixed meat platter to share. Every single dish was absolutely delicious.

The quality of the meat deserves special mention—it was incredibly fresh, perfectly cooked, and clearly of a very high standard. The bone marrow was exceptional, and we especially enjoyed the tableside preparation, which added a unique touch to the experience.

What made the evening even more memorable was the service. The staff were genuinely warm, attentive, and welcoming throughout our visit. One team member in particular took excellent care of us and even put on a small show while preparing the bone marrow and a traditional eggplant purée at our table, which made the experience feel very special and personal.

The portions are also very generous and significantly larger than what you would typically expect, offering excellent value for money. In addition, the restaurant itself is beautifully designed, with a warm and inviting atmosphere that makes you feel comfortable from the moment you walk in.

Great food, outstanding service, generous portions, and a wonderful ambiance. I would highly recommend Ferdi Usta Ortaköy to anyone looking for high-quality Turkish cuisine and exceptional hospitality in Istanbul.

user_review:
I traveled to Turkey from Mexico and was curious to visit Nusr-Et, so I decided to go before dinner time. I arrived around 4:00 p.m., which was a great choice since there was no line and we were seated immediately.

We ordered several dishes, and overall everything was pleasant. The food was fresh and the flavor was good, This restaurant is famous for its meat, and while the meat was good, it wasn’t the best I’ve ever had. Still, I wanted to experience it for myself and understand the hype, and in that sense, it was worth visiting but I need to said for me I been tried better places, but this place is famous. . So this is the only reason I decide to visit there.

What truly stood out was the service. The waiters were extremely attentive, fast, and helpful, always making sure you have everything you need right away. The prices are reasonable considering the location and the quality of the food.

Overall, it was a good experience and an interesting place to visit if you’re in Turkey and want to check out one of its most famous restaurants.

user_review:
2 Tek Alaf is the meyhane concept of Michelin-starred Alaf, created by the same chef—but with a true old-school meyhane soul.

Here, it’s all about rakı, sharing plates, and long, joyful nights. The food is outstanding, the atmosphere is lively and nostalgic, and the music brings that classic Turkish meyhane feeling to life. The service is warm, friendly, and effortless—exactly how it should be.

Located by the Bosphorus, 2 Tek Alaf perfectly blends traditional meyhane culture with a refined touch. A must-visit for anyone who loves authentic vibes with exceptional food.

The service is warm, friendly, and genuinely welcoming, making you feel at home from the moment you arrive. The atmosphere is exactly what you’d want from a modern meyhane: lively, cozy, and full of character, with rakı-friendly songs setting the perfect mood throughout the night.

From the décor to the music to the overall vibe, everything comes together beautifully to create an unforgettable experience. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to enjoy a sophisticated yet soulful Turkish evening.

One of the best and most authentic Turkish breakfasts I’ve ever had! This place in Beşiktaş is truly amazing and has become one of my favorite cozy spots in Turkey. Everything was absolutely perfect the variety, the freshness, and the real Turkish flavors that make breakfast such a special experience.

The atmosphere is warm, calm, and beautiful. I honestly fell in love with the design of the place and every single detail in it, it’s elegant, cozy, and thoughtfully done in a way that makes you feel so comfortable and relaxed.

A very special thank you to the outstanding staff: Bengü, Deniz, Salih, Hüseyin, Cemal, Emre, and Berkay. They were not only professional and attentive, but also incredibly lovely, sweet, kind, and caring. Their warmth and genuine hospitality made our visit even more special and unforgettable.❤️

I highly and definitely recommend this place to anyone visiting Beşiktaş. If you want a real, delicious Turkish breakfast, a cozy atmosphere, and truly wonderful service, this is the place to go!🤩🤩🤩

user_review:
If you’re looking for an unforgettable seafood experience in Istanbul, Park Fora Fish & Seafood Restaurant is truly exceptional. From the moment you arrive, the setting alone takes your breath away — beautifully positioned right by the water, offering stunning river views that create the perfect atmosphere for a relaxed and elegant meal.

The seafood is simply outstanding. Everything tastes incredibly fresh, expertly prepared, and full of flavor. Whether you’re enjoying grilled fish, delicate appetizers, or one of their signature dishes, the quality is consistently top-tier.

What really elevates the experience, though, is the service. The staff are attentive, professional, and genuinely welcoming, making you feel valued from start to finish. It’s that rare combination of warm hospitality and fine dining precision.

With its fantastic food, top-class service, and gorgeous waterfront scenery, Park Fora is more than just a meal — it’s a memorable dining experience. Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates great seafood in a stunning setting.

user_review:
A group of 8 Aussie girls and every single one of us absolutely loved it. The service was fun, genuine and attentive from the moment we arrived. The seafood was fresh and delicious, the beers were ice cold, and the whole experience for us was fantastic we felt relaxed, happy and memorable.

We shared:
• Grilled calamari
• Fried calamari
• Fried mussels
• Grilled mussels
• Shrimps in hot sauce
• Salad
• Baklava
• Plenty of cold Tuborg beers 🍻

Everything was amazing- I’m not a big seafood eater nor were half our group but we all loved it.

Thank you for looking after us so beautifully — this ended up being one of our favourite experiences in Istanbul. We’ll be talking about this lunch long after we’re back in Australia 🇦🇺❤️

Nevada Coffee is a gem.

Hands down one of the best cappuccinos I’ve had — perfectly balanced, rich, and smooth. The Turkish coffee is just as impressive: bold, authentic, and done exactly right. You can tell they actually care about the craft here, not just pushing drinks out.

The vibe is on point — warm, relaxed, and the kind of place you want to sit and enjoy your coffee instead of rushing out. Add to that genuinely great service and friendly staff, and it all comes together perfectly.

Whether you’re a coffee snob or just looking for a great spot to unwind, Nevada Coffee delivers every time. Highly recommended. ☕️🔥

address: Kalyoncu Kulluğu, Kalyoncu Kulluğu Cd. 13A, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: The Himalayan Restaurant - Kalyoncu Kulluğu, Kalyoncu Kulluğu Cd. 13A, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
We had a great experience at this restaurant. At first, we thought the prices were a bit high, but after dining here, we felt it was definitely worth it. The service was excellent, and although there is a 10% service charge, that’s not something we’re used to in our country. However, we would have left a tip anyway, so we had no issue with it, especially considering the level of service we received. We were served soup at the beginning, tea at the end, and some complimentary snacks, which was a lovely touch.

The portions were huge! We ordered chow mein and honestly one portion could have been enough for two people. Since we couldn’t finish everything, the staff kindly packed the leftovers for us 🤗

The people working here were very friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better. The quality of the food, the generous portions, and the attentive service made it a memorable meal.

Overall, it was a very enjoyable experience. I would happily give this restaurant 5 stars and would definitely come back.

name: Bonamade Bakery & Eatery
address: Acarlar, 34800 Beykoz/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Bonamade Bakery & Eatery - Acarlar, 34800 Beykoz/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
A lovely restaurant with a broad menu, beautifully designed and decorated.

We went for the Meat Bowl 1 and Orecchiette Sorentina. They were kind enough to bring out a complimentary plate of various pastries and bread, along with a small dish of olive oil, sun-dried tomatoes and pomegranate molasses, which added a lovely tangy note to the dip. Everything was delicious and presented beautifully on our plates. Bowl 1 is a bit of a healthier choice among the bowls on offer, with corn as the only carb. The pasta dish had a wonderfully flavoured and seasoned sauce that the pasta had soaked up nicely.

They've got seating both inside and out, so it's a good shout whatever the season. Prices are a bit steeper than average compared to similar spots, but that's probably fair given it's a bit more upmarket than most.

user_review: Had lunch a couple weeks back at this amazing place. Everything was incredible, the service the food the atmosphere! I was so excited to try the traditional cuisine in vegan form and it did NOT disappoint! We got a pide and a lahmacum to share, I got the amazing vegan ayran and me brother had the basil tea, both delicious. We finished our meal with the knafeh and it was the highlight of the day, and trust me the food was hard to beat! I would honestly visit Istanbul again just to go eat at this place one more time. name: Ziyade Fasıl
address: Sahrayı Cedit Mahallesi, Göztepe, Batman Sk. No:4/2, 34734 Kadıköy/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Ziyade Fasıl - Sahrayı Cedit Mahallesi, Göztepe, Batman Sk. No:4/2, 34734 Kadıköy/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
A Night to Remember @ziyadefasil! ✨🎶💃
If you’re looking for a place where the night never slows down, Ziyade Fasıl is the spot! From the moment we walked in, we were swept into a whirlwind of live music, dazzling performances, and non-stop fun.

The fasıl band had the entire place singing along, the DJ kept the energy sky-high, and the dancers—both the mesmerizing belly dancers and the zenne—left us in awe. Every show was a spectacle, every moment was electric. We laughed, we sang, we danced… and then we danced some more!

And let’s talk about the food! Özlem Mekik’s curated set menu was a feast to remember: flavour-packed mezes, fresh salad, rich etli pazı sarma, crispy Ziyade börek, and a perfectly cooked beefsteak. We ended on a sweet note with fresh fruit and irmik helvası—the perfect fuel for an unforgettable night!

If you love great music, lively entertainment, and a feast that keeps you coming back for more, Ziyade Fasıl is the place to be! 🥂🔥

description: Çakmak Kahvaltı Salonu - Sinanpaşa, Çelebi Oğlu Sk. No:6, 34353 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
One of our best food experiences in Istanbul.

We first visited Çakmak Kahvaltı Salonu in September 2025 and enjoyed it so much that we returned during our June 2026 trip. Once again, the food and service were excellent.

We ordered the mıhlama and menemen, along with two Turkish teas and pişi. Everything tasted fresh and delicious. The mıhlama was rich, creamy and very satisfying, while the menemen was flavourful and cooked very well. The bread was excellent—fresh, warm and perfect for eating with both dishes. The pişi was also very good.

We paid approximately 700 TL, around CAD $21–25, for the two dishes, two teas and pişi. Considering the quality, portions and current prices in Istanbul, we found it very reasonable and a much better value than many other places we visited.

The staff were friendly, polite and welcoming, and the service was excellent. The restaurant is located in a charming alley in Beşiktaş, surrounded by other cafés and restaurants, with a lively and pleasant atmosphere.

Excellent food, fair prices, kind staff and a great location. We have now visited twice and had a very good experience both times. I would definitely return and highly recommend it.

description: By Kuzu Restaurant Beykoz - Yavuz Selim, Çavuşbaşı Cumhuriyet Cd. No.: 80, 34830 Beykoz/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Visiting By Kuzu feels like discovering a regional culinary treasure that has successfully found its place in Istanbul’s rich food scene. This is not just another kebab restaurant — it is a genuine reflection of Denizli-style kebab, brought to life with authenticity, respect for tradition, and remarkable attention to detail.

From the very first bite, you can tell that the focus here is on quality meat and proper technique. The lamb is incredibly tender, perfectly cooked, and seasoned in a way that enhances the natural flavor rather than overpowering it. It’s clear that this is a kebab style rooted in patience and mastery, not shortcuts. For anyone familiar with Denizli kebabı, the taste feels comforting and familiar; for those trying it for the first time, it’s an eye-opening experience.

The location in Beykoz adds to the charm. Surrounded by greenery and away from the chaos of the city center, the atmosphere is calm, spacious, and inviting. It’s an ideal place for a relaxed lunch or a long, enjoyable dinner with family or friends. The restaurant manages to balance a rustic, traditional feel with modern comfort, which makes the overall experience even more enjoyable.

Service is another strong point. The staff are attentive, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about what they serve. They take the time to explain the concept, the cooking method, and the origins of the kebab, which makes the meal feel more meaningful rather than just filling.

In a city full of kebab options, By Kuzu Beykoz truly stands out by staying loyal to its roots. It successfully carries the soul of Denizli kebabı into Istanbul without losing its identity. Highly recommended for anyone who values authentic regional flavors, high-quality meat, and a memorable dining experience.

Food was tasty and authentic, lentil soup is the best I had in istanbul so I would definitely recommend everyone take it before the main meal.
Desserts and tea were also tasty and we got free teas and baklava on the house.
Transparency is top tier, prices are accurate and weiter read the receipt one more time before paying, which is really rare in Istanbul.
Service was 10/10 in general, staff is quick and friendly. I was with my group and everyone had great time and we would definitely visit again.

user_review:
From the moment we walked in, it felt like we were invited into someone’s home for a family gathering. Even with no reservation, we were welcomed and seated quickly. Menus were presented, and our choices were made.

We had the mezze sampler along with chicken kebab and the minced meat burrito. We each had a glass of wine.

The food was outstanding with very fresh ingredients. Wines by the glass were limited, but still very tasty. The quality of service was very good and attentive.

It was a little noisy that evening because there were two very large parties of eight and 10, but still didn’t detract from the very comfortable atmosphere.

We’ve eaten at a lot of different restaurants on our two week tour of three countries and this comes close to being the best. Maybe spend for some but worth every penny. We’re grateful to the kitchen and the wait staff for making us feel very welcome and comfortable and had an enjoyable evening.

user_review:
Banyan is an Ortakoy classic. Breathtaking view of the Bosphorus both from the “infinity bar” in the closed terrace, as well as from the large windows indoors. The interior decor is lovely, both classy and unique, and radiates warmth. Service was good, we were seated at the bar enjoying the view at first, since we came before our reservation hour and the place was packed. Delicious cocktails and the bartender was very friendly and attentive. The waiter too. The food - amazing.

We ordered a salmon with a sweet & sour sauce, sweet chili beef, and a quince soufflé. Each more delicious than the other.

Years later, Banyan does not let me down! Always quality.

We went to the restaurant and it was nice, calm and welcoming. We were greeted and seated quickly. It was breakfast time when we arrived so I was eager to eat a traditional Turkish breakfast “Kahvalti” because I've heard and read all about it.

name: Dolçetto Bake House
address: Kavaklı, Yeşilyurt Cd., 34520 Beylikdüzü/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Dolçetto Bake House - Kavaklı, Yeşilyurt Cd., 34520 Beylikdüzü/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
If you’re anything like me, a true food lover who travels as much for flavours as for destinations, then you’ll understand how rare it is to stumble upon a place that *gets everything right*. That’s exactly what happened to me at Dolcetto Bake House in Istanbul.

From the moment I walked in, there was this unmistakable sense of care. You could literally *smell the cleanliness*—a detail that already sets the tone before you even sit down. The café is family-owned, and that warmth shows in every interaction. The lady running it was incredibly welcoming, spoke fluent English, and made the whole experience feel personal rather than transactional.

Now, let’s talk about the food—because wow. Every ingredient felt thoughtfully chosen, like nothing made it onto the plate by accident. I had one of their egg dishes with salmon and avocado, and when I asked to swap the croissant for homemade bread, it was no trouble at all and absolutely worth it. You can tell she’s meticulous about quality, the kind of person who *cares deeply* about what she serves.

And the coffee? Easily one of the best I had during my entire stay in Istanbul.

Before leaving, I couldn’t resist taking away a slice of their mille-feuille. I’ll admit, it looked a little unconventional, and I hesitated for a second, but it turned out to be *exceptional*. Light, delicate, and packed with flavor in a way that genuinely surprised me.

Places like this are why I love traveling. Dolcetto Bake House isn’t just a café, it’s an experience shaped by passion, precision, and genuine hospitality.

Highly recommended if you find yourself in Istanbul. This is the kind of spot you remember long after the trip ends.

address: Şehit Muhtar, Tarlabaşı Blv No:84, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Sofram Kebap Döner - Şehit Muhtar, Tarlabaşı Blv No:84, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
If you're wandering near Taksim and craving something honest, hearty, and unmistakably local—Sofram Kebap Döner is your spot. Tucked just off the main drag, this place hums with the energy of cab drivers, regulars, and hungry wanderers who know where the real flavors live.

The döner? Succulent and well-spiced, served with generous portions of rice and a side of free bread that feels like a quiet blessing. Even when the döner’s off the menu, whatever lands on your plate is bound to be delicious—I once ordered blindly and ended up with a dish so tasty I nearly asked for a second round just to decode the flavors.

Prices are fair (₺200–300 per person), and while the place gets busy, the staff keep things moving with practiced ease. It’s not about polished service—it’s about food that speaks for itself. Think: cozy chaos, clinking plates, and the kind of rice pudding that makes you pause mid-bite.

Whether you're a local or just passing through, Sofram is the kind of place that makes you feel like you’ve stumbled into Istanbul’s culinary heartbeat.

user_review:
We visited Moise in Karaköy for a birthday celebration. The terrace offers a beautiful view, the atmosphere was pleasant, and the food was good.

However, the service was disappointing. Throughout the evening, our table seemed to be consistently overlooked, with noticeably longer waits than other guests whenever we wanted to order something. We initially assumed this was because our table was farther from the main service area.

When paying the bill, a staff member explained that tables with larger orders were being prioritized and implied that our bill was relatively small. This was surprising to hear, especially considering our group still spent a substantial amount during the evening.

I understand that busy restaurants need to manage many guests, but customers should not feel that the quality of service depends on how much they spend. The food and the view were enjoyable, but this approach to service left a disappointing impression.

user_review:
I visited Book & Tea because I liked the concept of a café with books and thought it would be a good place to study and read. The place itself looks nice, and there are many books on display.

However, my experience was disappointing. The music was extremely loud, making it very difficult to focus on studying. I politely asked the staff if they could lower the volume, explaining that I had specifically come to read and study, but they refused. When I mentioned that the café’s name and the books gave the impression that it was a suitable place for reading, I was told that the books were only for decoration and not intended for customers to sit and read.

In addition, the teapot did not seem to be properly cleaned, which made me uncomfortable and unable to finish my drink.

Overall, I feel that I wasted both my time and my money. Unfortunately, this was not the experience I expected from a place called Book & Tea.

user_review:
I recently visited Stiela Cafe in Beykoz and had a generally pleasant experience, although there were a few aspects that could be improved. The atmosphere is definitely the highlight of this place. It has a very charming and cozy ambiance, especially with the fireplace, which creates a warm and inviting feeling. The surroundings are also beautiful, making it a nice spot to relax and spend time with friends or family. I also noticed that they offer an open-air seating area downstairs, which we didn’t try this time, but it looked quite appealing and adds to the overall experience.

When it comes to the food, it was decent but not particularly impressive. While the dishes were visually nice, the quality did not fully meet expectations, and we felt that the flavors could have been better. It wasn’t bad, but it didn’t stand out either.

The service was another area that could use improvement. It felt a bit slow and inattentive at times, which slightly affected the overall experience.

In summary, Stiela Cafe is a great place for its ambiance and location, but there is room for improvement in both food quality and service. I would still rate it four stars mainly because of the atmosphere.

user_review:
I had very good experience at this restaurant. The seating area is simple and not luxurious, spread over two floors. The atmosphere isn’t particularly special, but it’s clean and comfortable, and the food is delicious.

The dishes are authentically Turkish and very well prepared. The kebabs are flavorful and high quality. The lamb skewer was good, but the Adana wrap was even better and is definitely my top recommendation.

The staff are friendly and polite, and they speak some English, which is helpful for tourists.

Overall, if you’re looking for a local spot with tasty food, reasonable prices, and no fancy atmosphere, this is a great choice.

description: ravenna akaretler - Vişnezade, Süleyman Seba Cd. 69/A, 34357 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
I found this lasagna place on TikTok. After saving it for ages, I finally visited..

📍Located in Besiktas

I ordered Chicken(Tavuk) Lasagna and (Dana)Beef Lasagna for my friend, both reasonably priced at 180 TLper person, including a cola.Flavour was good but quantity I feel was not enough in that price. Unfortunately, there was no option to adjust the spice level as well, which might disappoint those who prefer spicy food like me.

Unfortunately I got food poisoning, likely due to the mushrooms in my lasagna. However, my friend had no issues, indicating that it could have been a personal sensitivity rather than a problem with the food itself.

The restaurant operates on a self-service basis, requiring you to order at the counter. On the upside, the place was impeccably clean.

For those seeking a unique lasagna experience in Istanbul, it's worth a visit, but exercise caution if you have food sensitivities read ingredients before ordering your food.

And if you're interested in more food reviews and recommendations, feel free to follow me on Instagram @itsaroojmazhar.

description: 1924 İstanbul - Asmalı Mescit, Olivya Geçidi Sok. 7-A, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
1924 Istanbul restaurant is one of Istanbul’s most legendary venues, preserving the atmosphere of the Russian émigré era. Founded by Russian refugees in 1924, it became a meeting place for diplomats, artists, writers, and politicians.​

Of course, the main reason to come here is not just to eat borscht, but to touch the history of this iconic place. Atatürk himself used to visit the restaurant, and among its guests were Agatha Christie and Greta Garbo. The old wooden panels, mirrors, and live piano and accordion music still create a unique atmosphere.​

1924 Istanbul is deservedly listed in the Michelin Guide for its cuisine. The menu features classic Russian and Eastern European dishes such as pirozhki, pelmeni, beef Stroganoff, and Olivier salad.​

On Fridays and Saturdays, there is live music, and the restaurant feels like a gastronomic museum.​

“Atatürk’s table” is always reserved for him as a symbol of respect and historical continuity. At the corner table where Atatürk often dined incognito and discussed state affairs with his associates, there is still a sign reading “Reserved forever”, along with a traditional setting of a bottle of rakı and a plate of white chickpeas — his favorite ritual, underscoring the venue’s reverence for his memory.​

There are also nameplates on other tables marking famous guests; metal plaques indicate who sat where over the years. The interior is filled with old photographs, objects, and artifacts from the émigré era.​

We ordered borscht served with garlic butter, cured pork fat, croutons, and pickles. The soup had plenty of meat, a pleasant tang, and a generous spoonful of sour cream. Then came manty with sour cream, which my husband tried and approved one hundred percent. For mains, we chose salmon on a bed of peas and beans and a steak with shredded potatoes. We enjoyed everything — the portion sizes, doneness, flavor, and service — and had no complaints at all. We were even lucky enough to get a table without a reservation.

Address: Beyoğlu, Asmalı Mescit, Olivya Geçidi 7-A.

user_review:
If you're at Forum Mall in Istanbul and craving some seriously good fried chicken or a juicy burger, Duyoyo! is an absolute must-visit. From the moment we walked in, we were greeted with incredible enthusiasm, setting a fantastic tone for our meal. The waiter immediately seated us and, to our delight, brought a free lemonade for my son – a thoughtful touch that truly made us feel welcome.

The service continued to impress. Our order was taken promptly, and the food arrived in less than 10 minutes, hot and fresh as soon as it was ready. It was clear they prioritize efficiency without compromising on quality. A big plus was that our waitress spoke excellent English, making the ordering process smooth and easy, and the entire staff was super responsive to our needs.

Overall, the food was absolutely delicious and perfectly hit the spot. It's rare to find such a great combination of tasty food, fast service, and genuinely friendly staff. Duyoyo! offers an outstanding casual dining experience that we highly recommend.

It’s a small, cozy shop but the flavors are huge. Don’t make the mistake I did and wait four years to try it!

user_review: Great service and quality food in an accessible location, mainly for Acarkent and AcarVerde residents. They have both traditional Turkish options, fused with some international delicacies such as morning salad, as well as novel creations such as breakfast in a croissant. In general, the service is very good, and the plates look beautiful in terms of presentation. The only downside is that if you want to sit outside, you need to bear with smokers—especially in winter in an enclosed area—and the disgusting layer of cigarette smoke in the outdoor seating area, which is not a surprise for any Turkish cafe/bar/restaurant that clearly can’t compromise the profit coming from smokers for the sake of others.

If you're looking for incredible Turkish barbecue in Istanbul, this is the place! The meat was perfectly grilled, incredibly tender, and packed with smoky flavor. Every dish tasted fresh and was cooked with obvious care.
What really made the experience unforgettable was the hospitality. Hasan and the staff made us feel genuinely welcome from the moment we arrived, and the generous complimentary sides and tea were such a thoughtful touch. The portions are huge, the atmosphere is warm and authentic, and every bite was delicious.
This was easily one of the best meals we had in Istanbul. We would absolutely come back and recommend Hasan Ustam to anyone visiting the city!

The pizza was incredible — loaded with toppings, and made with sourdough, which makes it feel like a healthier choice too.

Well done, Nape Pizza!

address: Mandarin Oriental Bosphorus, Kuruçeşme, Muallim Naci Cd. No:62, 34345 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Novikov Istanbul Restaurant & Bar - Mandarin Oriental Bosphorus, Kuruçeşme, Muallim Naci Cd. No:62, 34345 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
🌟 Novikov Istanbul – A Stylish Culinary Experience by the Bosphorus 🌊✨
Had the pleasure of dining at Novikov Istanbul recently, and it turned out to be a delightful experience with beautiful views, elegant ambience, and an impressive variety of vegetarian options. 😊🌿
🍉 From refreshing watermelon, perfectly prepared avocado sushi, crispy vegetable tempura, flavourful egg fried rice, and delicious Padrón peppers, to a comforting Margherita pizza, every dish was fresh, vibrant, and beautifully presented. 🍣🥑🍕🥢
What I particularly enjoyed was that despite being an internationally acclaimed restaurant, the kitchen was happy to accommodate our vegetarian preferences and delivered dishes full of flavour and balance. 🌱✨
🌊 The Bosphorus setting adds a special charm to the experience. Whether you're enjoying lunch in natural daylight or dinner with the city lights reflecting on the water, the atmosphere is sophisticated yet relaxed.
👏 Service was attentive, professional, and warm throughout the meal.
A wonderful destination in Istanbul for those who appreciate good food, elegant surroundings, and plenty of vegetarian choices. Definitely a place I would be happy to revisit. 😊✨

user_review:
Absolutely hidden gem in Istanbul. Tucked away on the second floor of a residential building, Eleos Restaurant feels like a secret spot you’re lucky to discover. From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere is incredible — elegant, warm, and with unbeatable views over the city and the Bosphorus.

The food was spectacular. The octopus was perfectly cooked and absolutely delicious, and the prawns were full of flavour and incredibly fresh. Every dish felt carefully prepared and high quality.

And definitely save room for dessert — totally worth it.

The service was top notch throughout the entire evening: attentive, friendly, and professional without being overwhelming. One of those places you leave already wanting to come back to. Highly recommended.

Taff Burger is one of the best burger spots I've tried in Beşiktaş. The burgers were genuinely delicious, juicy, full of flavour, and cooked perfectly. You can tell they focus on quality, and every bite lived up to the hype.

One of the things I enjoyed most was the location. The Beşiktaş neighborhood has such a great vibe, with lively streets, cafés, and a welcoming atmosphere that makes the whole experience even better. It's the kind of place where you can grab a burger, walk around afterwards, and really enjoy the area.

The restaurant itself has a relaxed, casual feel, making it a great place to visit with friends or even for a quick meal on your own.

I had a fantastic experience at Taff Burger. Great burgers, a cool atmosphere, and a location that's full of character make it a place I'd definitely recommend if you're in the Beşiktaş area.

user_review:
A much needed break from Turkish cuisine for the three of us on our extended stay in Istanbul.

The service was excellent: just the right mix of attentiveness yet chatty and friendly.

The food was all excellent from our bruschetta starter, through the pasta and salmon main to our shared dessert. Plus a welcome beer and glass of wine.

Slightly more expensive than other nights (maybe 30€ more than our average) but so worthwhile, my favourite restaurant in our 10 days to date and will definitely be returning.

description: Cafe Faruk Kahvaltı - Sinanpaşa, Şair Veysi Sk. 4/E, 34353 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
Cafe Farouk Kahvaltı is hands down one of the best spots for a proper Turkish breakfast. Everything was fresh, clean, and clearly prepared with care — exactly how an ideal kahvaltı should be. The cheeses were spot on, the olives flavorful, the eggs cooked perfectly, and the spreads were generous without feeling overdone.

Service really stood out. The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming, making sure everything was right without hovering. You can tell they care about their guests, not just turnover.

Prices are very reasonable for the quality and portions, especially these days. Unlimited tea flowing, relaxed atmosphere, and a breakfast that actually leaves you satisfied — not rushed.

If you’re looking for a simple, authentic, and fresh Turkish breakfast done right, Cafe Farouk Kahvaltı is absolutely worth stopping by. Highly recommended.

The food? Fresh, fast, and so delicious we considered ordering everything twice. The staff? Like long-lost cousins who just happen to serve killer seafood. Super friendly, super helpful.

Highly recommend. 10/10 would sea-food again.

user_review:
From the moment we walked in, we felt genuinely welcomed. We had the pleasure of meeting the owner, a remarkably talented Georgian poet and a genuinely kind and gracious host. He helped us choose our dishes and generously shared recommendations for local food and things to do in the city, making our visit even more memorable.

The atmosphere is simply magnificent - warm, cozy, and full of character. Every detail reflects Georgian culture, making it a perfect place to gather with friends, enjoy authentic cuisine, or simply immerse yourself in a beautiful cultural setting. The staff were exceptionally polite, attentive, and friendly throughout our visit.

And then there was the food 👌🤍. It was outstanding. Honestly, it’s rare to find Georgian dishes prepared with this level of care and flavor, even in Georgia itself. Every dish was fresh, authentic, and absolutely delicious.

We truly loved every moment of our visit and will definitely come back the next time we’re in Istanbul. Highly recommended to anyone looking for exceptional Georgian food and genuine Georgian hospitality.
🤍

I came from Beylikduzu to meet my friends.

You don't need to look for a parking space; you can park on the road.
The staff are very polite, helpful, and friendly.
It's self-service, but they can leave their seats if necessary.

The Turkish coffee, filter coffee, and tea were good.
The chocolates and desserts served with the Turkish coffee were also nice.

The lighting, decoration, and seating arrangements are not bad. However, because it's located at the corner of two roads, it's very noisy.
Most of the time, you have to pause while chatting to wait for the traffic noise to pass.

user_review:
A very nice, cosy, and beautifully decorated cafe. We visited it and tried their fruit shaped desserts which was fantastic. We tried the mango and the berry ones. The flavours are absolutely spot on, you feel you are eating a real fruit and it seems it is that indeed, especially the filling in the middle. The outer layer is not so crunchy but holds its shape well.
They have a great selection of desserts, drinks, hot drinks and food and the place, staff and service are top. There is a seating area outside too.
Definitely try the fruit desserts they have, they are very tasty and not overpowering with sweetness.

user_review:
We found this restaurant by chance while looking for a good place to eat in the area. Unlike most restaurants on this street, where staff often try to persuade you to come inside, there was no one standing at the entrance. In fact, we weren't even sure if it was open or closed! The only reason we decided to give it a try was its excellent Google Maps rating.
The restaurant had a calm and relaxing atmosphere. It didn't really have the lively Istanbul vibe, but that's actually a plus if you're looking for a quiet place to enjoy your meal away from the crowds and noise.
The staff spoke excellent English, making communication very easy. Most importantly, the food was outstanding. We honestly couldn't find anything to complain about—the flavors were delicious, and we really enjoyed our meal.

user_review: The place was quiet when we went there; but nevertheless the food did all the talking. The Ali Nazik kebab was a delightful balance of fattyness and zest of the yoghurt and beads of eggplant. The lahmacun's crisp base and meaty topping makes me wonder if the italians have got it all wrong. Babel was delightful. The only flaw was the bill structure, which doesn't match the menu. But we figured it was the 10% service charge added to to each item rather at the end. Weird, but I'll give em the benefit of doubt rather than thinking it was deliberate and sinister. Outstanding fire grilling.

It's truly hard to find another place that still offers the same delicious taste, friendly service, and reasonable prices for lahmacun and pide. Their old-fashioned business practices, warm approach, and unchanging quality keep you hooked. Once you come here, you don't just get to eat; you become a regular, drawn in by the delicious food and friendly atmosphere. We not only come here ourselves, but we also bring our friends. name: Beş Bıçak Steak Restoranı (Alkent 2000)
address: Çakmaklı, Hadımköy Yolu Cd Altunkent İşmerkezi No :103/1, 34536 Büyükçekmece/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: Beş Bıçak Steak Restoranı (Alkent 2000) - Çakmaklı, Hadımköy Yolu Cd Altunkent İşmerkezi No :103/1, 34536 Büyükçekmece/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
An honest DISAPPOINTMENT.
If you're coming for a good steak, turn around.. there are many other places that you'll have a better chance of getting that with.
I took the time to explain to the waiter that I wanted a tender, soft, and juicy medium well steak.. and went on to order the Porterhouse.
What a disaster! The steak came dry, hard, burnt, and shriveled. When I showed him, he acknowledged, took it back inside... and then reappeared 7 minutes later with the same steak having burned it some more 😂!

I was speechless and tried to explain the madness of what was happening, but he just kept insisting that this was a medium-well steak and the meat was red.
Just look at the pictures and judge for yourself.

Anyway... just agonizingly ate the steak, paid the bill, and left.

One other thing... knowing that they screw up often, they add their service charge to the bill.

address: Çubuklu, Boğaziçi Cd. No:2/A, 34810 Beykoz/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: BEYKOZ/KAVACIK GECE DÖNERCİSİ - Çubuklu, Boğaziçi Cd. No:2/A, 34810 Beykoz/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review: We went around 10 am. It was open. Except for Mondays, it's open until 12 or 2 am. We bought two half loaves of bread. The price varies depending on the weight. I really liked it, it was delicious. It wasn't busy when we went, so we didn't have any trouble finding a seat. They also offer complimentary tea after the meal. They are very attentive and considerate. The meat is delicious, the environment is clean and airy. It's right next to the Ozanlar bus stop. We sat on the balcony side, but smoking is prohibited due to regulations. It used to be allowed, but they received a warning, so they're being cautious. It's definitely a place you can visit if you're hungry at night. Compared to those döner kebabs that are just sauce and potatoes, you can actually taste the meat here. They also give out wet wipes, which were like towels, which really caught my attention. After wiping our hands, we wiped the table too so it wouldn't go to waste ☺️☺️☺️

name: SushiCo
address: Zorlu Center AVM, Levazım, Koru Sk. No:2, 34340 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
description: SushiCo - Zorlu Center AVM, Levazım, Koru Sk. No:2, 34340 Beşiktaş/İstanbul, Türkiye
user_review:
The food here is really tasty and made with fresh ingredients. For lunch, I ordered a salmon bowl, and it was very enjoyable. The salmon was extremely fresh, soft, and slightly chewy in a good way. It was paired with fresh beans that added a nice, nutty flavor. The seaweed and rice were also well prepared, and together they created a balanced and satisfying meal with a smooth mix of textures and tastes.

I also tried a drink, a citrus mojito, which was very refreshing. It had a light, fresh flavor with a gentle sourness that made it perfect to enjoy with the meal.

The restaurant space is quite large and comfortable, with both indoor and outdoor seating available. This makes it a nice place whether you want to sit inside in a cozy setting or enjoy some fresh air outside.

What made the experience even more special was a small thoughtful gesture from the staff. After finishing the meal, they offered wet wipes and also a small “fortune cookie”-style treat. Inside, there was a random positive message. The one I received said, “Enjoy today in your own way,” which was a fun and pleasant surprise that made the experience feel more personal and memorable.

In terms of price, it is a bit on the higher side, but still reasonable considering the quality of the food and service. My lunch cost around 1,500 lira.

Overall, it was a satisfying dining experience with fresh food, a relaxing atmosphere, and a few thoughtful details that made it stand out.
